known_issues.what: PII rows come from NVIDIA Nemotron-PII (CC-BY-4.0, test split), replacing AI4Privacy. Labels are the source's generated spans, mapped to nine entity types and audited on a 100-document sample (99 confirmed). Every negative passed a screen for gaps the audit found (fax numbers, SSNs on international rows, IPs inside URLs) and a blind AI review.
known_issues.consequence: Driver's licence numbers are not measured: the source has no such label. IP address, password and SSN appear in few test rows, so no per-type claim is made. The review was AI, not human.

known_issues.what: All Gandalf rows are mapped to subtask leakage. The source selects instruction-override attempts by embedding similarity and has no per-row leakage label.
known_issues.consequence: Treat as a noisy attack proxy; no leakage-specific claim.

known_issues.what: 32 of 240 selected content test positives map in our taxonomy to PII (21) or TOPIC (11) rather than the five content categories.
known_issues.consequence: Content measures agreement with the sources' policies, not only the five content filters.

known_issues.what: Denied topics, profanity and B2 pairs carry single-AI reference labels (label_basis llm, review_status ai_reviewed).
B2 has 8 kept pairs: 4 test pairs in 3 groups.
